scope: local-only; no AWS writes; not browser Apply/Save/Reload proof

results.summary: The design presents a coherent end-to-end dynamic pricing architecture with per-product elasticity, competitor ingestion, segment-aware decisioning, guardrail enforcement, experimentation, and analytics tied to operational controls.

findings.title: Per-product and per-segment pricing pipeline is well-aligned
findings.explanation: The architecture connects context ingestion, competitor collection, feature normalization, elasticity serving, and decision publication in a coherent loop that matches the pricing workflow and keeps the pricing decision service as the policy-enforced control point.

findings.title: Experimentation and analytics are integrated into the operating loop
findings.explanation: The design routes decision and outcome events into analytics, then surfaces results in the operations console and policy store, which supports controlled A/B testing and review before broader rollout.

results.summary: The design provides a coherent ML pricing pipeline with elasticity inference, competitor intake, segment-aware pricing, guardrails, experimentation, dashboards, and explicit freshness/compliance controls.

findings.title: Clear end-to-end pricing decision path
findings.explanation: The architecture cleanly connects request intake, context/feature retrieval, elasticity inference, policy enforcement, publication, and outcome recording, which directly matches the pricing-engine workflow.

findings.title: Operational feedback loop is well integrated
findings.explanation: Decision, context, and experiment outcomes are sent to analytics, warehouse, and monitoring, giving the system a coherent learning and review loop rather than a one-way pricing path.

findings.title: Scalable SKU/segment processing strategy
findings.explanation: Stable SKU/segment partitioning, bounded consumers, and freshness monitoring show an architecture intended to handle the 100k+ SKU constraint without centralizing all updates on the request path.

results.summary: The design covers the required pricing loop, experiment analytics, guardrails, freshness controls, and 100k+ SKU scaling with a coherent separation of online decisioning from offline model work.

findings.title: Explicit per-product elasticity estimation is well covered
findings.explanation: The design separates the elasticity model, serving layer, and the online decision flow, which makes the predictive core easy to reason about and evolve.

findings.title: Experiment analysis path is clearly linked to rollout governance
findings.explanation: Accepted prices and outcomes flow into analytics, and the operations console uses those results to gate broader rollout, which supports controlled A/B testing.

findings.title: Operational freshness controls are embedded in the context path
findings.explanation: The context processor and monitoring both track freshness and queue age, giving a credible mechanism for the five-minute update objective.

results.summary: The architecture covers the full dynamic-pricing scope with explicit online decisioning, elasticity inference, competitor/context ingestion, experimentation, guardrails, and operational visibility.

findings.title: Per-SKU pricing flow is well separated from offline model training
findings.explanation: The design cleanly splits online pricing decisions from offline training, registry, and artifact management, which reduces coupling and keeps the request path focused on decision latency.

findings.title: Freshness and operational signals are explicitly tracked end to end
findings.explanation: Monitoring covers API health, decision freshness, processor delay, and serving health, which gives operators the signals needed to manage real-time pricing behavior and stale-input recovery.

findings.title: Governed experiment and release path supports pricing strategy rollout
findings.explanation: Experiment outcomes flow into analytics, while model training, registry, and artifact storage keep reviewed versions explicit before they are served online.

results.summary: The architecture covers the full dynamic-pricing scope: elasticity estimation, competitor and inventory context, segment-aware pricing, guardrails, experimentation, analytics, and governed rollout for 100k+ SKUs with freshness and compliance controls.

findings.title: Per-SKU and per-segment pricing path is well decomposed
findings.explanation: The design separates context ingestion, feature preparation, elasticity serving, decisioning, policy persistence, and operations reporting. This keeps the online path narrow while supporting offline learning and analytics.

findings.title: Freshness and fallback behavior are explicit
findings.explanation: The processor and monitoring path track queue age and end-to-end freshness, while the decision service retains the last approved price when context or policy is stale. That directly supports the real-time update objective.

findings.title: Governed model lifecycle reduces release risk
findings.explanation: Model training, registry, artifacts, and serving are separated so the online decision path only consumes reviewed elasticity versions. This is a maintainable and auditable approach for ML-driven pricing.

results.summary: The design presents a coherent real-time multilingual sentiment platform with clear ingestion, inference, trend analytics, reporting, alerting, and review loops that cover the published core scope.

findings.title: End-to-end real-time sentiment pipeline is well decomposed
findings.explanation: The design has a coherent ingestion, streaming, scoring, persistence, analytics, reporting, and alerting flow with clear responsibilities and provenance preservation.

findings.title: Multilingual model and review loop address hard NLP cases
findings.explanation: The architecture does not treat sarcasm, slang, emoji, or low-confidence predictions as afterthoughts; it includes a dedicated multilingual model, uncertainty routing, and adjudicated labeling for improvement.

findings.title: Trend and alerting path supports both reports and shift detection
findings.explanation: Trend analytics, reporting storage, console access, and qualified shift notifications are connected in a way that supports both automated reporting and actionable alerting.

results.summary: The design covers the full sentiment-analysis scope with multilingual, aspect, emotion, sarcasm, reporting, and alerting flows, while keeping real-time scoring separate from offline training and historical analytics.

findings.title: End-to-end real-time path is explicitly bounded
findings.explanation: The design connects ingestion, stream processing, version-pinned serving, and durable result writes with explicit latency monitoring on the accepted-post-to-score path, which directly supports the under-2-second constraint.

findings.title: Multilingual and sarcasm-aware modeling is carried through training, serving, and review
findings.explanation: The model, labeling, training, and registry flow consistently preserves multilingual, slang, emoji, and sarcasm signals rather than treating them as afterthoughts.

findings.title: Trend and alert pipeline is decoupled from online scoring
findings.explanation: Trend analytics, reporting, and notifications consume scored events asynchronously, which keeps the online scoring path focused on latency while still supporting reports and shift alerts.

results.summary: The design provides a coherent real-time sentiment platform with multilingual inference, aspect and emotion detection, trend analytics, alerting, reporting, review, and monitoring aligned to the published core scope.

findings.title: Multilingual sentiment and sarcasm pipeline is well aligned to the core ML scope
findings.explanation: The design closes the loop from source normalization to multilingual inference, human review, offline training, registry gating, and monitoring. This directly supports the requested sentiment, emotion, aspect, sarcasm, trend, and reporting behaviors.

findings.title: Operational path separates online scoring from slower reporting and review flows
findings.explanation: The architecture keeps review, reporting, and historical aggregation asynchronous while preserving a low-latency online scoring path. That is a strong fit for real-time sentiment analysis under the stated latency target.

results.summary: The design covers real-time sentiment ingestion, multilingual aspect and emotion inference, trend detection, reporting, and alerting with a coherent online/offline split and strong monitoring support.

findings.title: Real-time pipeline is well decomposed across ingestion, streaming, inference, and persistence
findings.explanation: The architecture cleanly separates source adapters, webhook ingestion, durable buffering, stream normalization, model serving, and downstream analytics/reporting. This supports both low-latency scoring and asynchronous trend/report workloads without overloading the online path.

findings.title: Multilingual, sarcasm-aware modeling is explicitly represented
findings.explanation: The model, serving layer, and human-review loop all preserve language and context signals, which is a strong fit for slang, emojis, sarcasm, and multi-language support.

findings.title: Change-point analytics and alerting support sentiment shift detection
findings.explanation: Trend analytics produces thresholded shift events and the notification service adds deduplication and evidence context, which is appropriate for significant sentiment-shift alerts.

results.summary: The design cleanly covers real-time multilingual sentiment, aspect, emotion, sarcasm, trend, reporting, and alerting requirements with a coherent training-to-serving loop and monitoring for latency and accuracy targets.

findings.title: Broad core scope is covered by the online and offline ML pipeline
findings.explanation: The architecture includes source connectors, durable ingestion, stream normalization, multilingual inference, trend analytics, reporting, alerts, labeling, training, registry, and monitoring, which together cover the stated sentiment-analysis workflow end to end.

findings.title: Model governance and rollback path are well-defined
findings.explanation: The registry, training, and monitoring path is explicit about versioning, held-out evaluation, promotion gates, and rollback to the previous approved model, which strengthens operational safety for the sentiment models.

findings.title: Trend reporting and shift alerting are connected to scored-event outputs
findings.explanation: Scored results feed both the analytics pipeline and the reporting store, while qualified change-point events are routed to notifications. This provides a coherent path from online scoring to offline reporting and alerting.

results.summary: The design covers the full demand-forecasting scope, including multigranularity output, hierarchical reconciliation, probabilistic intervals, cold-start handling, and automated model selection, while also addressing the stated accuracy and batch-runtime constraints.

findings.title: Strong end-to-end support for forecasting lifecycle
findings.explanation: The submission connects ingestion, point-in-time feature creation, model selection, probabilistic training, 90-day batch inference, hierarchy reconciliation, and governed read access into a coherent forecasting system. The same run/version lineage is preserved through storage and serving, which supports both operational use and auditability.

results.summary: The design covers the full forecasting scope, including multi-granularity outputs, hierarchy reconciliation, cold-start handling, calibrated intervals, and explicit MAPE/runtime gates for 100k+ SKU-location daily reforecasting.

findings.title: Cold-start and model-selection path is unusually explicit and well constrained
findings.explanation: The design separates sparse/new SKU handling from normal series routing, uses history sufficiency rules, and preserves evidence for selection and promotion decisions. This reduces ambiguity around new-product forecasting and automated model selection.

findings.title: Hierarchical reconciliation is connected end-to-end
findings.explanation: Bottom-level daily forecasts and uncertainty samples flow into a dedicated reconciler, which uses versioned hierarchy matrices and calendar rules before publishing coherent outputs.

findings.title: Feature lineage supports leakage-safe training and inference
findings.explanation: The design keeps point-in-time features, as-of external vintages, and immutable raw history, which is a strong fit for forecasting with promotions, holidays, weather, and economic signals.

results.summary: The architecture strongly covers the demand forecasting brief: multi-granularity and hierarchical forecasts, exogenous and promotional signals, cold-start support, probabilistic outputs, and explicit gates for accuracy, scale, and batch runtime are all represented in the component graph.

findings.title: No material core gaps identified
findings.explanation: The submitted architecture covers the published forecasting scope, hierarchy handling, exogenous signals, cold-start support, interval output, and the operational constraints for accuracy, scale, and batch runtime with coherent component responsibilities and flows.

findings.title: End-to-end forecasting path is well partitioned
findings.explanation: The design separates ingestion, point-in-time feature creation, model selection/training, batch scoring, reconciliation, publication, and read access, which makes the workflow understandable and implementable.

results.summary: The design covers the full forecasting workflow end to end, including multi-granularity outputs, hierarchical reconciliation, cold-start support, probabilistic intervals, and operational gates for accuracy and batch runtime.

findings.title: Cold-start product path is well integrated
findings.explanation: The design does not treat new-product forecasting as a separate afterthought; it routes sparse or zero-history SKUs through attribute/analog and hierarchy-prior logic in both training and batch inference, which supports the core requirement directly.

findings.title: Hierarchical coherence is preserved through reconciliation and monitoring
findings.explanation: The reconciler produces store/region/national-consistent outputs from bottom-level forecasts, and monitoring checks hierarchy-sum violations and freshness before release, which strengthens the coherence of published results.

findings.title: Probabilistic outputs are carried end-to-end
findings.explanation: Intervals are not only generated during training; they are calibrated, reconciled, persisted as quantiles, and exposed to users, reducing the risk that uncertainty is lost after model execution.

results.summary: The design covers the full forecasting scope, including multi-granularity outputs, hierarchical reconciliation, exogenous signals, cold-start handling, probabilistic intervals, and automated model selection with explicit quality gates.

findings.title: Explicit cold-start path for new SKUs
findings.explanation: The design does not just mention new-product forecasting; it routes sparse or zero-history items through a dedicated attribute/analog plus hierarchy-prior path before normal model selection.

findings.title: End-to-end hierarchical coherence is preserved
findings.explanation: Base forecasts are reconciled against versioned hierarchy matrices and the monitoring layer checks hierarchy-sum violations, which directly supports coherent store/region/national outputs.

results.summary: The design covers the full demand-forecasting scope, including multigranularity output, hierarchical reconciliation, probabilistic intervals, cold-start handling, and automated model selection, while also addressing the stated accuracy and batch-runtime constraints.
